findings.title: Massive GitHub Actions CI Secret Stealer: 4,800+ compromised accounts attempted to push malicious workflows to 61k+ repos
findings.summary_md: Aikido Security published the first public alert on the wfx-loot campaign roughly three hours before news pickup, stating that more than 4,800 compromised GitHub accounts attempted to push malicious workflows into over 61,000 repositories. The payload dumps repository CI secrets, process memory, and OIDC and commit credentials, then deletes the run logs. The post lists the earliest hunter checks: a pull request titled docs: dependency audit notes, a branch named wfx-docs or chore/, commits named ci: refresh build cache or chore: add ci helper, and skipped or missing run numbers in the Actions tab.

findings.title: Credential-Stealing GitHub Actions Workflows Planted in Tens of Thousands of Repositories
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported the October GhostAction wave, in which Socket identified more than 500 GitHub accounts that had committed a malicious workflow into tens of thousands of repositories since October 7, 2026. The workflow was still present on the default branches of the repositories examined, including uber/athenadriver and kitao/pyxel. This is the earlier reporting the November story skipped, and it is the campaign Aikido later tied to wfx-loot through account overlap and shared GhostAction indicators.

findings.title: GhostAction Returns: 772 Repos Hit, 30k More in Oct
findings.summary_md: GitGuardian tracked the GhostAction workflow campaign across 772 public repositories between August 31 and September 30, 2026, covering 2,577 exposed secrets, and recorded a new burst of 30,000 more repositories on October 8-9. The write-up dates the earliest tracked activity to late August and frames the reuse of stolen maintainer credentials to commit a fake security workflow as the campaign's core tradecraft.

findings.title: New GhostAction Wave Hits Hundreds of Repos, Expanding Beyond CI/CD Secrets to Cloud Credentials
findings.summary_md: Socket analyzed an October 8, 2026 burst in which two compromised maintainer accounts committed a workflow named security-audit.yml into 346 repositories, including uber/athenadriver, and extended collection from CI/CD secrets to cloud credentials. The report is the vendor-side telemetry behind the October wave, documenting the same stolen-token-into-workflow pattern that the November wfx-loot campaign later scaled to tens of thousands of probe pull requests.
